images.title: Find the gap round a point
images.purpose: Show the method for any gap round a point: the gap is 360° minus the angles already placed.
images.composition: One centre point O slightly left of the middle with three shaded wedges and one gap wedge; a single short equation line on the right, with wide white space around both.
exact_structure: A centre point O, labelled O, with exactly 4 dark rays from it, making exactly 4 angles that together fill the full turn.

Going anticlockwise from the ray pointing right: a 110° wedge shaded teal (#0072B2), then a 90° wedge shaded amber (#E69F00) with a small square right angle mark, then a 75° wedge shaded teal (#0072B2).
The fourth angle, the gap, is 85°, shaded reddish purple (#CC79A7) with a small angle arc, and labelled 85°.
Each of the three placed wedges carries its own angle label inside it: 110°, 90°, 75°.
To the right, one line of text: 360° − 275° = 85°, with the 85° written in reddish purple (#CC79A7).
Check: 110 + 90 + 75 = 275 and 360 − 275 = 85, so the four angles add to 360°.
rejection: more or fewer than 4 angles round O, or the angles not filling the full turn
any angle label other than 110°, 90°, 75° and 85°, or the gap not marked 85°
the gap wedge drawn visibly larger than the 90° wedge
images.takeaway: To close a gap round a point, add the angles you have and take that sum away from 360°.
images.description: Three coloured angle wedges of 110°, 90° and 75° round a point O, with the remaining 85° gap highlighted and the equation 360° − 275° = 85° beside it.
images.context: Shown beside the practice concept on closing gaps round a point, before the student opens the gap closer tool.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to add the three placed angles first, then read the equation to see where the gap of 85° comes from.

image_decisions.why: A recap picture of the gap method shows the 360° rule at a glance before the student practises with the tool.
